sources.cite: Microsoft Learn, Blob rehydration from the archive tier
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Relevant text: rehydrate by copying to an online tier (the source stays in archive, no early deletion fee) or by Set Blob Tier; standard priority 'might take up to 15 hours to complete for objects under 10 GB', high priority 'might complete in less than one hour for objects under 10 GB' (costs more, for emergencies); a pending standard request can be raised to high; archive blobs should stay 180 days or pay early deletion; a 10 GiB per hour per account rehydration limit. The SAS overview (read 2026-11-18): a SAS gives delegated access to specific resources, with chosen permissions and start and expiry times, without sharing the account key; a user delegation SAS is recommended; use short expiry times. That making the container public exposes every blob to anyone is the author's statement.
